turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, ma'am, but I don't know if I should call her, she's been so kind to me, but I don't know her very well, and I wouldn't want to intrude.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, come in and play with this boy. I will not be ignored.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know if I'm supposed to play with Miss Havisham's niece. I don't want to do anything wrong, and my sister would be worried if I got into any trouble here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, do not stand there like a statue. Take this boy by the hand and lead him to the conservatory. We will play a game, all of us, together.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know how to play the games you have in mind, and I wouldn't want to disappoint you or make a fool of myself.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, do not hesitate, take the boy's hand and lead him away. I will not be thwarted by his awkwardness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I'm not sure I should be taking part in any games or activities here, especially if it might be a burden on you or Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be ignored, boy. Take Estella's hand and follow her, at once!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't wish to trouble you or Miss Havisham, and I fear I might not be suitable company for you, especially Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, do not let the boy escape your grasp. I will not have him insulting my hospitality with his feeble excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't mean to cause any trouble, Miss Havisham, but I fear I'm not the right sort of company for you or Estella. I'm just a simple boy from the village, and I don't know if I'd be suitable for games or activities.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy! You think you know what is suitable for me? I will be the judge of that.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I don't think I can play the games you mentioned, as I'm not very good at them, and I fear I might make a fool of myself in front of you and Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You shall play with me, Pip, and you shall play with Estella, and you shall not refuse, lest you incur my displeasure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I don't know if I can play the games you mentioned, as I don't have any proper clothes to wear, and I wouldn't want to make a mess of things in front of you and Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence, Pip! You dare to question my judgment and my generosity? I shall provide you with clothes, and you shall play with me, and you shall be grateful.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I don't know if I can play the games as you wish, as I'm not sure I'm worthy of your generosity, and I fear I might be a disappointment to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not dare to question my generosity, Pip. I have made a sacrifice for you, and you will not turn your back on me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I don't mean to be ungrateful, but I'm not sure I know how to play the games you have in mind, and I fear I might make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn the games, Pip, and you will play them with me, because it is my will, and you will do as I say.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
